# ADR-0002 · Isolation of structural parsing

> [!NOTE]
> **Proposed.** Under discussion — nothing here is decided yet.

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-09-07
- **Kind:** Mechanism
- **Decision:** OPT-1 — Bounded work in-process — an instruction and allocation budget the scanner checks itself
- **Assumes:** [ADR-0001 · Structural PDF parsing](ADR-0001-structural-pdf-parsing.md)
- **Decides:** [PDF verification · AC-8](../pdf-service/pdf-verify.md#ac-8)
- **Source:** [`ADR-0002-isolation-of-structural-parsing.adr.yaml`](../../../trace-fixtures/ADR-0002-isolation-of-structural-parsing.adr.yaml)

## Question

Where does the byte scanner run, given that it must not be able to exhaust the service on a malformed upload?

## Forces

- ADR-0001#R-4 places structural parsing off the request thread under default JVM limits.
- A malformed cross-reference chain is unbounded work until a limit stops it.
- blast_radius is medium: the verification scope is called by other scopes in this system.

## Decision

**OPT-1** — Bounded work in-process — an instruction and allocation budget the scanner checks itself

Reversibility: reversible

## Obligations

What the decision obliges the implementation to do.

- **R-1** — Fix the budget as policy, not caller-supplied, on the same grounds the spec states for max_size_bytes.
- **R-2** — Map budget exhaustion to invalid_xref_trailer, not to a new identifier. AC-10's list is closed.

## Accepted costs

- A malformed upload can still cause an allocation spike visible to concurrent requests.

## Revisit when

- p99 verification latency under malformed input exceeds 200 ms, against the 34 ms measured on well-formed input in 2026-08. The shared-heap argument no longer holds and OPT-2 returns.
- A second scope in this system begins parsing untrusted bytes, so the budget is no longer the only thing standing between an upload and the request path.

## Options considered

|  | Option | Reversibility |
|---|---|---|
| **OPT-1** (chosen) | Bounded work in-process — an instruction and allocation budget the scanner checks itself | reversible |
| OPT-2 | A separate process per upload, with rlimits | costly |

### OPT-1 · Bounded work in-process — an instruction and allocation budget the scanner checks itself (chosen)

References: metrics src/main/java/ch/adnovum/pdfservice/VerificationMetrics.java

- **D-1** — Bounds the malformed-input case, but shares a heap with the request path, so an allocation spike is still felt service-wide.
- **D-2** — One counter and one timeout, both already exposed by the existing metrics.
- **D-3** (EUR/month of compute) — 0 — the budget is checked inside the existing request path.

### OPT-2 · A separate process per upload, with rlimits

References: mechanism <https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/setrlimit.2.html>

- **D-1** — A hard boundary; the kernel enforces it rather than the code being trusted to.
- **D-2** — Adds process lifecycle, a byte channel and a second failure mode (spawn failure) that AC-10's identifier list has no room for.
- **D-3** (EUR/month of compute) — Roughly 900/month: one process spawn per upload, plus the memory floor of a second JVM for every concurrent upload. The largest single line in the option.

## Dimensions

What every option was judged against.

- **D-1** — A hostile upload must be able to exhaust its own budget only, never the service's.
- **D-2** — Operational surface: a mechanism nobody can observe or tune is a mechanism nobody will maintain.
- **D-3** — Decisive here: the option that costs materially more per upload has to earn it on D-1. *(unit: EUR/month of compute; basis: B-1; source: platform chargeback 2026-H2)*

## Basis

The quantities the dimensions are stated under.

|  | Quantity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| B-1 | 40000 uploads / month | ingest telemetry, 2026-08 monthly mean |
